newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Slow start to vote in Moroccan referendum.
newsitem.headline: Slow start to vote in Moroccan referendum.

text.p: Polling started slowly in Morocco on Friday at 8 a.m. (0800 GMT) in a referendum to change the nation's constitution and set up a second house of parliament.
White flags bearing the legend "Referendum, 13 September" fluttered in bright sunshine outside booths as they opened in the capital Rabat.
There was little sign of early voters in the poll in which some 12 million Moroccans are eligible to take part.
Among early voters at a central booth in the city, was Mohamed Taled, a teacher aged about 40. "I came to vote because it is a national duty," he said.

King Hassan, whose paramount powers will not be touched, has called for a 'yes' vote for the change whose main effect will be to split the present 333-seat Majlis Anuwab (Chamber of Representatives) in two to strengthen regional representation.
The second house will have power to force a vote of no-confidence in the government.
"The king has asked us to take part in the referendum. That is why I am here," said Fatima Zohra Wahit, a civil servant from the health ministry, outside another polling booth.

Voting, which will include more than 118,000 people in the disputed Western Sahara, is due to end at 6 p.m. (1800 GMT), with first results late on Friday night and the final tally being known on Saturday.
